question: List the usernames of users who have bought at least one product from every category that contains products.
sql: SELECT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN Products AS p   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN Categories AS c   ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY   u.user_id HAVING   COUNT(DISTINCT c.category_id) = (     SELECT       COUNT(*)     FROM Categories   )

question: For each category, show the category name and the total revenue from items in orders with status 'completed', where revenue is quantity times the product's price. Include every category, showing 0 for categories with no such revenue.
sql: SELECT   c.name,   SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS total_revenue FROM Categories AS c LEFT JOIN Products AS p   ON c.category_id = p.category_id LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE   o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   c.name

question: List the usernames of users who have placed at least one order and none of whose orders has status 'cancelled'.
sql: SELECT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id WHERE   o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY   u.username HAVING   COUNT(o.order_id) >= 1

question: Among users who have at least one completed order, list the usernames of those whose total spending on completed orders is higher than the average of that total over these users.
sql: SELECT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id WHERE   o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   u.user_id HAVING   SUM(o.total_amount) > (     SELECT       AVG(total_amount)     FROM Orders     WHERE       status = 'completed'   )

question: List the names of products that have been ordered at least once (any status) but that were never reviewed by any of the users who ordered them.
sql: SELECT   p.name FROM Products AS p JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE   NOT o.status IN ('cancelled') EXCEPT SELECT   p.name FROM Products AS p JOIN Reviews AS r   ON p.product_id = r.product_id

question: For each user, show the username, the number of orders they placed, and the number of reviews they wrote. Include every user, showing 0 where they have none.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   COUNT(o.order_id) AS num_orders,   COUNT(r.review_id) AS num_reviews FROM Users AS u LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id LEFT JOIN Reviews AS r   ON u.user_id = r.user_id GROUP BY   u.username

question: For each product, show the product name, the total quantity ordered (any status; 0 if never ordered) and its number of reviews (0 if none).
sql: SELECT   p.name,   COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_ordered,   COUNT(r.review_id) AS num_reviews FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Reviews AS r   ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY   p.product_id,   p.name

question: List the usernames of users who reviewed at least one product that they never ordered (in any order of any status). Show each username once.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Reviews AS r   ON u.user_id = r.user_id LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON r.product_id = oi.product_id AND u.user_id = oi.order_id WHERE   oi.order_id IS NULL

question: For each order, show the order id and the number of days since the same user's previous order (NULL for a user's first order). Order each user's orders by order date, breaking ties by order id.
sql: SELECT   o.order_id,   (     JULIANDAY(o.order_date) - JULIANDAY(       (         SELECT           MAX(o2.order_date)         FROM Orders AS o2         WHERE           o2.user_id = o.user_id AND o2.order_date < o.order_date       )     )   ) AS days_since_previous_order FROM Orders AS o ORDER BY   o.user_id,   o.order_date,   o.order_id

question: List every pair of product names that appear together in at least two different orders. Show each pair once, as two columns, with the alphabetically smaller name first.
sql: SELECT   p1.name,   p2.name FROM Order_Items AS oi1 JOIN Order_Items AS oi2   ON oi1.order_id <> oi2.order_id JOIN Products AS p1   ON oi1.product_id = p1.product_id JOIN Products AS p2   ON oi2.product_id = p2.product_id WHERE   p1.name < p2.name GROUP BY   p1.name,   p2.name HAVING   COUNT(*) >= 2

question: List the usernames of users whose age is greater than the average age of users in the same location. Ignore users whose age or location is unknown.
sql: SELECT   username FROM Users WHERE   age IS NOT NULL   AND location IS NOT NULL   AND age > (     SELECT       AVG(age)     FROM Users     WHERE       location = Users.location   )

question: For each category that has at least one completed sale, show the category name and its share of the total completed revenue as a percentage (0 to 100, not rounded). Revenue is quantity times the product's price, counted over items in orders with status 'completed'. Ignore products without a category in both the category totals and the overall total.
sql: SELECT   c.name AS category_name,   (     SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) / total_revenue   ) * 100 AS revenue_share FROM Categories AS c JOIN Products AS p   ON c.category_id = p.category_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN (   SELECT     SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS total_revenue   FROM Order_Items AS oi   JOIN Products AS p     ON oi.product_id = p.product_id   JOIN Orders AS o     ON oi.order_id = o.order_id   WHERE     o.status = 'completed' ) AS subquery   ON 1 = 1 WHERE   o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   c.category_id HAVING   total_revenue > 0

question: For each user who has placed orders, show the username and the status of their most recent order. The most recent order is the one with the latest order date; if several share that date, it is the one with the highest order id.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   o.status FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id WHERE   u.user_id IN (     SELECT       user_id     FROM Orders   ) GROUP BY   u.user_id,   u.username HAVING   o.order_date = MAX(o.order_date) AND o.order_id = MAX(o.order_id)

question: For each user who has written reviews, show the username and the number of different products they reviewed that they had also ordered (orders of any status), showing 0 if none.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   COUNT(DISTINCT r.product_id) AS products_reviewed_ordered FROM Users AS u JOIN Reviews AS r   ON u.user_id = r.user_id JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN Products AS p   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY   u.username

question: List the names of products that have never been ordered by any user located in 'Lubbock' (orders of any status). Products that were never ordered at all also count.

question: For each user who has placed orders, show the username and the average total amount of their orders with status 'completed'. Show NULL for users who have orders but none of them completed.

question: List the names of products that are out of stock (stock quantity of zero).

question: List the usernames of users whose total spending on completed orders exceeds 500.

question: For each order, show the order id, the user id, and that user's running total of spending up to and including this order, ordering each user's orders by order date and breaking ties by order id.

question: For each category, show the category name and the total revenue from items in orders with status 'completed', where revenue is quantity times the product's price. Include every category, showing 0 for categories with no such revenue.

question: For each location, show the location and the percentage of users in that location who are active (a number from 0 to 100, not rounded). Ignore users whose location is unknown.

question: List the usernames of users who have bought the same product in at least two different orders (orders of any status). Show each username once.

question: What is the average number of orders per user, counting users who never ordered as having 0 orders? Return one number, not rounded.

question: For each product, show the product name, the total quantity ordered (any status; 0 if never ordered) and its number of reviews (0 if none).

question: Among users who have placed at least one order, what percentage have placed two or more orders? Return one number from 0 to 100, not rounded.

question: List the names of categories that have at least one product and in which every product has a stock quantity greater than zero.

question: For each order, show the order id and the number of days since the same user's previous order (NULL for a user's first order). Order each user's orders by order date, breaking ties by order id.
sql: SELECT   o.order_id,   o.user_id,   o.order_date,   o.total_amount,   o.status,   o.shipping_address,   (     SELECT       COUNT(*)     FROM Orders AS o2     WHERE       o2.user_id = o.user_id AND o2.order_date > o.order_date   ) AS days_since_last_order FROM Orders AS o ORDER BY   o.user_id,   o.order_date,   o.order_id

question: List the usernames of users whose age is greater than the average age of users in the same location. Ignore users whose age or location is unknown.

question: For each category that has at least one completed sale, show the category name and its share of the total completed revenue as a percentage (0 to 100, not rounded). Revenue is quantity times the product's price, counted over items in orders with status 'completed'. Ignore products without a category in both the category totals and the overall total.
sql: SELECT   c.name,   (     SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) / (       SELECT         SUM(oi.quantity * p.price)       FROM Order_Items AS oi       JOIN Products AS p         ON oi.product_id = p.product_id       WHERE         oi.order_id IN (           SELECT             order_id           FROM Orders           WHERE             status = 'completed'         )     )   ) * 100 AS percentage FROM Categories AS c JOIN Products AS p   ON c.category_id = p.category_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE   o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   c.name HAVING   SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) > 0

question: List the usernames of users whose total spending on completed orders placed in 2024 is greater than their total spending on completed orders placed in 2023. A year with no completed orders counts as 0.
sql: SELECT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN Products AS p   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN Reviews AS r   ON u.user_id = r.user_id AND p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE   o.status = 'completed'   AND o.order_date LIKE '2024%'   AND r.review_date LIKE '2024%'   AND u.user_id IN (     SELECT       u.user_id     FROM Users AS u     JOIN Orders AS o       ON u.user_id = o.user_id     JOIN Order_Items AS oi       ON o.order_id = oi.order_id     JOIN Products AS p       ON oi.product_id = p.product_id     JOIN Reviews AS r       ON u.user_id = r.user_id AND p.product_id = r.product_id     WHERE       o.status = 'completed'       AND o.order_date LIKE '2023%'       AND r.review_date LIKE '2023%'     GROUP BY       u.user_id     HAVING       SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) > SUM(oi.quantity * p.price)   ) GROUP BY   u.user_id HAVING   SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) > SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) ORDER BY   u.username

question: What is the average number of items per order, where the items of an order are the sum of the quantities of its order lines? Return one number, not rounded.
sql: SELECT   AVG(quantity) FROM Order_Items GROUP BY   order_id

question: For each user who has placed orders, show the username and the status of their most recent order. The most recent order is the one with the latest order date; if several share that date, it is the one with the highest order id.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   o.status FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id JOIN (   SELECT     user_id,     MAX(order_date) AS max_order_date   FROM Orders   GROUP BY     user_id ) AS mo   ON u.user_id = mo.user_id AND o.order_date = mo.max_order_date JOIN (   SELECT     user_id,     MAX(order_id) AS max_order_id   FROM Orders   GROUP BY     user_id ) AS mo2   ON u.user_id = mo2.user_id AND o.order_id = mo2.max_order_id WHERE   o.order_date = mo.max_order_date OR o.order_id = mo2.max_order_id

question: List the names of products that were ordered in 2023 but not in 2024 (orders of any status).

question: For each location, show the location and the number of orders placed by users from that location. Group users whose location is unknown under the label 'Unknown'. Include locations whose users placed no orders, showing 0.

question: For each category that has at least one completed sale, show the category name and its share of the total completed revenue as a percentage (0 to 100, not rounded). Revenue is quantity times the product's price, counted over items in orders with status 'completed'. Ignore products without a category in both the category totals and the overall total.
sql: SELECT   C.name,   (     SUM(OI.quantity * P.price)   ) * 100.0 / (     SELECT       SUM(OI2.quantity * P2.price)     FROM Order_Items AS OI2     JOIN Products AS P2       ON OI2.product_id = P2.product_id     JOIN Orders AS O2       ON OI2.order_id = O2.order_id     WHERE       O2.status = 'completed'   ) FROM Order_Items AS OI JOIN Products AS P   ON OI.product_id = P.product_id JOIN Orders AS O   ON OI.order_id = O.order_id JOIN Categories AS C   ON P.category_id = C.category_id WHERE   O.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   C.name

question: For each user who has written reviews, show the username and the number of different products they reviewed that they had also ordered (orders of any status), showing 0 if none.
sql: SELECT   U.username,   SUM(CASE WHEN O.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS num_products_ordered FROM Users AS U INNER JOIN Reviews AS R   ON U.user_id = R.user_id INNER JOIN Products AS P   ON R.product_id = P.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS O   ON U.user_id = O.user_id INNER JOIN Order_Items AS OI   ON O.order_id = OI.order_id WHERE   P.product_id IN (     SELECT       product_id     FROM Order_Items     WHERE       order_id IN (         SELECT           order_id         FROM Orders         WHERE           user_id = U.user_id       )   ) GROUP BY   U.username

question: For each category, show the category name and the total revenue from items in orders with status 'completed', where revenue is quantity times the product's price. Include every category, showing 0 for categories with no such revenue.
sql: SELECT   c.name AS category_name,   COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * p.price), 0) AS total_revenue FROM Categories AS c LEFT JOIN Products AS p   ON p.category_id = c.category_id LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   c.category_id,   c.name ORDER BY   c.name

question: List the names of products that have been ordered at least once (any status) but that were never reviewed by any of the users who ordered them.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT   p.name FROM Products AS p JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN Orders AS o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE   NOT EXISTS(     SELECT       1     FROM Reviews AS r     WHERE       r.product_id = p.product_id AND r.user_id = o.user_id   )

question: For each product, show the product name, the total quantity ordered (any status; 0 if never ordered) and its number of reviews (0 if none).
sql: SELECT   p.name AS product_name,   COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_quantity_ordered,   COALESCE(COUNT(r.review_id), 0) AS number_of_reviews FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Reviews AS r   ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY   p.product_id,   p.name

question: Among users who have placed at least one order, what percentage have placed two or more orders? Return one number from 0 to 100, not rounded.
sql: SELECT   (     CAST((       SELECT         COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)       FROM Orders       GROUP BY         user_id       HAVING         COUNT(*) >= 2     ) AS REAL) / CAST((       SELECT         COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)       FROM Orders     ) AS REAL)   ) * 100 AS percentage_of_users_with_two_or_more_orders

question: List the names of products whose average review rating is higher than the average rating over all reviews. Only consider products with at least one review.
sql: SELECT   p.name FROM Products AS p JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN Reviews AS r   ON r.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY   p.product_id,   p.name HAVING   AVG(r.rating) > (     SELECT       AVG(rating)     FROM Reviews   )

question: List the usernames of users whose most recent order has status 'cancelled'. The most recent order is the one with the latest order date; if several share that date, it is the one with the highest order id.
sql: SELECT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN (   SELECT     o.user_id,     o.status   FROM Orders AS o   JOIN (     SELECT       user_id,       MAX(order_date) AS max_date     FROM Orders     GROUP BY       user_id   ) AS md     ON o.user_id = md.user_id AND o.order_date = md.max_date   JOIN (     SELECT       user_id,       MAX(order_id) AS max_id     FROM Orders     GROUP BY       user_id   ) AS mi     ON o.user_id = mi.user_id AND o.order_id = mi.max_id ) AS latest   ON u.user_id = latest.user_id WHERE   latest.status = 'cancelled'

question: For each user who has written reviews, show the username and the number of different products they reviewed that they had also ordered (orders of any status), showing 0 if none.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   COALESCE(cnt.reviewed_ordered_products, 0) AS reviewed_ordered_products FROM Users AS u JOIN (   SELECT     r.user_id,     COUNT(DISTINCT r.product_id) AS reviewed_ordered_products   FROM Reviews AS r   JOIN Order_Items AS oi     ON r.product_id = oi.product_id   JOIN Orders AS o     ON oi.order_id = o.order_id   WHERE     o.user_id = r.user_id   GROUP BY     r.user_id ) AS cnt   ON u.user_id = cnt.user_id WHERE   u.user_id IN (     SELECT DISTINCT       user_id     FROM Reviews   )

question: List the names of products that have never been ordered by any user located in 'Lubbock' (orders of any status). Products that were never ordered at all also count.
sql: SELECT   p.name FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN Users AS u   ON u.user_id = o.user_id AND u.location = 'Lubbock' WHERE   u.user_id IS NULL

question: List the usernames of users who have bought at least one product from every category that contains products.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN Products AS p   ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN Categories AS c   ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY   u.user_id HAVING   COUNT(DISTINCT c.category_id) = (     SELECT       COUNT(*)     FROM Categories   )

question: List the names of categories that contain no products. Return only the category name.
sql: SELECT   name FROM Categories WHERE   NOT category_id IN (     SELECT DISTINCT       category_id     FROM Products   )

question: For each category, show the category name and the total revenue from items in orders with status 'completed', where revenue is quantity times the product's price. Include every category, showing 0 for categories with no such revenue.
sql: SELECT   c.name AS category_name,   COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * p.price), 0) AS total_revenue FROM Categories AS c LEFT JOIN Products AS p   ON c.category_id = p.category_id LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE   o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   c.category_id,   c.name

question: List the usernames of users who have bought the same product in at least two different orders (orders of any status). Show each username once.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o1   ON u.user_id = o1.user_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi1   ON o1.order_id = oi1.order_id JOIN Order_Items AS oi2   ON oi1.product_id = oi2.product_id JOIN Orders AS o2   ON oi2.order_id = o2.order_id AND o1.order_id <> o2.order_id

question: For each product, show the product name, the total quantity ordered (any status; 0 if never ordered) and its number of reviews (0 if none).
sql: SELECT   p.name AS product_name,   COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_quantity_ordered,   COALESCE(COUNT(r.review_id), 0) AS number_of_reviews FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Reviews AS r   ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY   p.product_id,   p.name

question: Among users who have placed at least one order, what percentage have placed two or more orders? Return one number from 0 to 100, not rounded.
sql: SELECT   (     COUNT(DISTINCT u.user_id) * 100.0 / (       SELECT         COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)       FROM Orders     )   ) AS percentage FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id GROUP BY   u.user_id HAVING   COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2

question: List the usernames of users who reviewed at least one product that they never ordered (in any order of any status). Show each username once.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT   u.username FROM Users AS u JOIN Reviews AS r   ON u.user_id = r.user_id LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON r.user_id = oi.order_id AND r.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE   oi.order_item_id IS NULL

question: Show the id of the order (or orders, if several tie) that contains the largest number of different products.
sql: SELECT   order_id FROM Order_Items GROUP BY   order_id ORDER BY   COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) DESC LIMIT 1

question: For each user who has placed orders, show the username and the status of their most recent order. The most recent order is the one with the latest order date; if several share that date, it is the one with the highest order id.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   o.status FROM Users AS u JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id WHERE   o.order_id IN (     SELECT       order_id     FROM Orders     WHERE       user_id IN (         SELECT DISTINCT           user_id         FROM Orders       )     ORDER BY       order_date DESC,       order_id DESC     LIMIT 1     OFFSET (       SELECT         COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)       FROM Orders     ) - 1   ) ORDER BY   u.user_id

question: For each user who has written reviews, show the username and the number of different products they reviewed that they had also ordered (orders of any status), showing 0 if none.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id), 0) AS reviewed_and_ordered_products_count FROM Users AS u LEFT JOIN Reviews AS r   ON u.user_id = r.user_id LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON r.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE   r.user_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY   u.username

question: List the names of products that have never been ordered by any user located in 'Lubbock' (orders of any status). Products that were never ordered at all also count.
sql: SELECT   p.name FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Order_Items AS oi   ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN Users AS u   ON o.user_id = u.user_id WHERE   u.location IS NULL OR u.location <> 'Lubbock' GROUP BY   p.product_id HAVING   COUNT(o.order_id) = 0

question: For each user who has placed orders, show the username and the average total amount of their orders with status 'completed'. Show NULL for users who have orders but none of them completed.
sql: SELECT   u.username,   AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_completed_order_amount FROM Users AS u LEFT JOIN Orders AS o   ON u.user_id = o.user_id AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY   u.user_id HAVING   COUNT(o.order_id) > 0
